Fonts.

This is a simple font manager that can be used to load fonts.

FontManager #

Bases: ResourceManager

A font manager for handling fonts in the game.

Supports both pygame.font and pygame.freetype font systems:

Examples:

Use default font system (pygame.font)#

font = FontManager.get_font()

Force pygame.font#

font = FontManager.get_font(use_freetype=False)

Force pygame.freetype#

font = FontManager.get_font(use_freetype=True)

Change default system#

FontManager.set_font_system(use_freetype=True) font = FontManager.get_font() # Now uses freetype by default

Check current system#

system = FontManager.get_font_system() # Returns "pygame" or "freetype"

class FontManager(ResourceManager):
    """A font manager for handling fonts in the game.

    Supports both pygame.font and pygame.freetype font systems:

    Examples:
        # Use default font system (pygame.font)
        font = FontManager.get_font()

        # Force pygame.font
        font = FontManager.get_font(use_freetype=False)

        # Force pygame.freetype
        font = FontManager.get_font(use_freetype=True)

        # Change default system
        FontManager.set_font_system(use_freetype=True)
        font = FontManager.get_font()  # Now uses freetype by default

        # Check current system
        system = FontManager.get_font_system()  # Returns "pygame" or "freetype"

    """

    OPTIONS: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {}
    RENDER_CACHE: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {}
    _font_cache: ClassVar[dict[str, GameFont]] = {}

    class FontProxy(FontEvents, ResourceManager):
        """A font proxy."""

        # A proxy belongs to its manager: each construction is a new one (ResourceManager)
        SHARES_INSTANCE: ClassVar[bool] = False

        def __init__(self: Self, game: object = None) -> None:
            """Initialize the font proxy.

            Args:
                game (object): The game object.

            """
            super().__init__(game=game)
            self.game: Any = game
            self.proxies: list[Any] = [self.game, pygame.freetype]

        @override
        def on_font_changed_event(self: Self, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
            """Handle font changed event.

            Args:
                event (pygame.event.Event): The event to handle.

            """
            self.game.on_font_changed_event(event)

    def __init__(self: Self, game: object = None) -> None:
        """Initialize the font manager.

        Args:
            game (object): The game object.

        """
        super().__init__(game=game)
        self.game: Any = game

        # Register pygame.freetype (imported at module top, so always available)
        pygame.freetype.init()
        log.info('Freetype Font Cache Size: %s', pygame.freetype.get_cache_size())
        log.info(
            'Freetype Font Default Resolution: %s',
            pygame.freetype.get_default_resolution(),
        )

        # Set up the default options.
        FontManager.OPTIONS['font_name'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_name']
        FontManager.OPTIONS['font_size'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_size']
        FontManager.OPTIONS['font_bold'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_bold']
        FontManager.OPTIONS['font_italic'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_italic']
        FontManager.OPTIONS['font_antialias'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_antialias']
        FontManager.OPTIONS['font_dpi'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_dpi']

        # Set font system based on command line argument
        font_system: str = self.game.OPTIONS.get('font_system', 'freetype')
        FontManager.OPTIONS['use_freetype'] = font_system == 'freetype'
        log.info('Font system initialized: %s', font_system)

        pygame.freetype.set_default_resolution(FontManager.OPTIONS['font_dpi'])

        # Ideas:
        #
        # Pre-generate font cache based on settings that are provided.
        # Indexed by the letter they represent.
        # a -> <font name>
        # What about bold, italic, bold + italic, anti-aliased?
        # Maybe we can generate all combinations?
        # Allow caller to pass in a font settings blob and generate.
        # A progress bar class that integrates with tqdm?

        # Ideally, I'd like to support both modes.
        #
        # https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/font.html
        # To use the pygame.freetypeEnhanced pygame module for loading
        # and rendering computer fonts based pygame.ftfont as pygame.fontpygame
        # module for loading and rendering fonts define the environment variable
        # PYGAME_FREETYPE before the first import of pygamethe top level pygame
        # package. Module pygame.ftfont is a pygame.fontpygame module for loading
        # and rendering fonts compatible module that passes all but one of the font
        # module unit tests: it does not have the UCS-2 limitation of the SDL_ttf
        # based font module, so fails to raise an exception for a code point greater
        # than 'uFFFF'. If pygame.freetypeEnhanced pygame module for loading and
        # rendering computer fonts is unavailable then the SDL_ttf font module
        # will be loaded instead.

        # Set up proxies: the font proxy first, then pygame.freetype
        self.proxies: list[Any] = [FontManager.FontProxy(game=game), pygame.freetype]

    @classmethod
    def args(cls, parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
        """Add font options to the argument parser.

        Args:
            parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The argument parser.

        Returns:
            argparse.ArgumentParser

        """
        group = parser.add_argument_group('Font Options')

        group.add_argument(
            '--font-name',
            default=DEFAULT_FONT_NAME,
            help=(
                f'Font to use (default: the bundled {DEFAULT_FONT_NAME}; the bundled variants are '
                "Vera, VeraBd, VeraIt and VeraBI; any other name is looked up among the system's "
                'fonts)'
            ),
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-size',
            type=int,
            default=14,
            help=(
                'size of the default font, used by text that asks for no font of its own '
                '(default: %(default)s)'
            ),
        )
        # Stored in FontManager.OPTIONS, but no font loader or renderer reads them yet
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-bold',
            action='store_true',
            default=False,
            help='not used yet: stored, but no text is drawn bold because of it',
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-italic',
            action='store_true',
            default=False,
            help='not used yet: stored, but no text is drawn italic because of it',
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-antialias',
            action='store_true',
            default=False,
            help='not used yet: stored, but each text widget chooses its own antialiasing',
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-dpi',
            type=int,
            default=72,
            help=(
                'the resolution, in dots per inch, freetype font sizes are scaled at (sets '
                "pygame.freetype's default resolution); the pygame font system ignores it "
                '(default: %(default)s)'
            ),
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-system',
            choices=['pygame', 'freetype'],
            default='freetype',
            help='Font system to use: freetype (enhanced, default) or pygame (built-in)',
        )

        return parser

    # PyInstaller-compiled games fall back to the bundled Vera.ttf font
    # since system font paths are not available in frozen environments.
    @classmethod
    def font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
        """Return a font object.

        If the font requested can't be found then bitstream_vera will be loaded instead.

        Note that if you are trying to package your game with pyinstaller, you'll need to bundle
        your game's fonts with the pyinstaller invocation.  Make sure you have distribution
        rights to the fonts you're including with your game.

        bitstream_vera is a permissively licensed font that can be used with your game.

        Args:
            font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

        Returns:
            GameFont

        """
        if not font_config:
            font_config = FontManager.OPTIONS

        # Provide default font configuration if not set
        if 'font_name' not in font_config:
            font_config['font_name'] = DEFAULT_FONT_NAME
        if 'font_size' not in font_config:
            font_config['font_size'] = 14

        # Create cache key
        cache_key = f'{font_config["font_name"]}_{font_config["font_size"]}'

        # Check cache first
        if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
            return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

        log.info('Loading Font: %s', font_config['font_name'])
        log.info('Font Size: %s', font_config['font_size'])

        # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
        font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=font_config['font_name'])
        if font_path is not None:
            loaded_font: GameFont = cast(
                'GameFont',
                pygame.freetype.Font(file=font_path, size=font_config['font_size']),
            )
            FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
            return loaded_font

        try:
            loaded_font = cast(
                'GameFont',
                pygame.freetype.SysFont(
                    name=font_config['font_name'],
                    size=font_config['font_size'],
                ),
            )
        except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
            # Note: Not sure why but pygame.freetype.SysFont doesn't
            # seem to work with pyinstaller packaged games.
            log.info('Loading Font: Built-In')

            # BUG: pygame's documentation claims that passing None as the font name
            # will load the default font, but this raises TypeError ("not a file object")
            # in PyInstaller-packaged games. Load the bundled Vera.ttf instead.
            # (BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY says where bitmappy.spec bundles it.) The fallback keeps
            # the requested size (it used to load at 12 whatever was asked for).
            loaded_font = cast(
                'GameFont',
                pygame.freetype.Font(
                    file=BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY / BUNDLED_FONT_FILE_NAMES['vera'],
                    size=font_config['font_size'],
                ),
            )

        # Cache the result
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    @classmethod
    def pygame_font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
        """Return a regular pygame font object for compatibility with UI components.

        Args:
            font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

        Returns:
            GameFont: A regular pygame font object.

        """
        if not font_config:
            font_config = FontManager.OPTIONS

        # Provide default font configuration if not set
        if 'font_name' not in font_config:
            font_config['font_name'] = DEFAULT_FONT_NAME
        if 'font_size' not in font_config:
            font_config['font_size'] = 14

        # Create cache key for pygame fonts
        cache_key = f'pygame_{font_config["font_name"]}_{font_config["font_size"]}'

        # Check cache first
        if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
            return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

        # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
        font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=font_config['font_name'])
        if font_path is not None:
            loaded_font: GameFont = cast(
                'GameFont',
                pygame.font.Font(font_path, font_config['font_size']),
            )
            FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
            return loaded_font

        try:
            # Try to load system font
            loaded_font = cast(
                'GameFont',
                pygame.font.SysFont(font_config['font_name'], font_config['font_size']),
            )
        except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
            # Fall back to default font
            loaded_font = cast('GameFont', pygame.font.Font(None, font_config['font_size']))

        # Cache the result
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    @classmethod
    def get_font(
        cls,
        font_system: Literal['pygame', 'freetype'] | None = None,
        font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> GameFont:
        """Get a font object, choosing between pygame.font and pygame.freetype.

        Args:
            font_system: Either "pygame" or "freetype". If None, use the default preference.
            font_config: The font configuration.

        Returns:
            pygame.font.Font | pygame.freetype.Font: The requested font object.

        """
        if font_system is None:
            # Default to freetype
            use_freetype: bool = bool(FontManager.OPTIONS.get('use_freetype', True))
        else:
            use_freetype = font_system == 'freetype'

        # Try freetype first, fall back to pygame if it fails
        if use_freetype:
            try:
                return cls.font(font_config)
            except (TypeError, FileNotFoundError, OSError) as e:
                log.info('Freetype font failed, falling back to pygame: %s', e)
                return cls.pygame_font(font_config)
        else:
            return cls.pygame_font(font_config)

    @classmethod
    def set_font_system(cls, font_system: Literal['pygame', 'freetype']) -> None:
        """Set the default font system preference.

        Args:
            font_system: Either "pygame" or "freetype" to specify the font system.

        """
        FontManager.OPTIONS['use_freetype'] = font_system == 'freetype'
        log.info('Font system set to: %s', font_system)

    @classmethod
    def get_font_system(cls) -> str:
        """Get the current font system preference.

        Returns:
            str: "freetype" or "pygame" indicating the current font system.

        """
        return 'freetype' if FontManager.OPTIONS.get('use_freetype', False) else 'pygame'

    @classmethod
    def compare_font_systems(
        cls,
        text: str = 'Hello World',
        size: int = 24,
    ) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        """Compare both font systems side by side.

        Args:
            text (str): Text to render for comparison.
            size (int): Font size for comparison.

        Returns:
            dict: Information about both font systems.

        """
        config: dict[str, Any] = {'font_size': size}

        # Get pygame.font. Its render takes (text, antialias, color) positionally, not
        # freetype's fgcolor keyword (which raised TypeError on a real pygame.font.Font).
        pygame_font = cast('pygame.font.Font', cls.get_font('pygame', config))
        pygame_surface: pygame.Surface = pygame_font.render(text, True, (255, 255, 255))  # ruff: ignore[boolean-positional-value-in-call]

        # Get pygame.freetype
        freetype_font = cls.get_font('freetype', config)
        freetype_render_result = freetype_font.render(text, fgcolor=(255, 255, 255))
        freetype_surface: pygame.Surface = (
            freetype_render_result[0]
            if isinstance(freetype_render_result, tuple)
            else freetype_render_result
        )

        return {
            'pygame': {
                'font': pygame_font,
                'surface': pygame_surface,
                'size': pygame_surface.get_size(),
                'type': 'pygame.font.Font',
            },
            'freetype': {
                'font': freetype_font,
                'surface': freetype_surface,
                'size': freetype_surface.get_size(),
                'type': 'pygame.freetype.Font',
            },
        }

def __getattr__(self: Self, attr: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    """Get an attribute from the first proxy that has it.

    This method is called when an attribute is not found.

    Args:
        attr: The attribute to get.

    Returns:
        The attribute.

    Raises:
        AttributeError: If no proxy has the attribute (or there are no proxies yet).

    """
    # The proxies themselves are an instance attribute: before __init__ sets them there are
    # none to try (looking them up here would recurse)
    if attr == 'proxies':
        raise AttributeError(MISSING_ATTRIBUTE_MSG.format(cls=type(self), attr=attr))

    # Try each proxy in turn (BUGS.md #198: the lookup returned or raised on the first)
    for proxy in self.proxies:
        try:
            return getattr(proxy, attr)
        except AttributeError:
            continue

    if self.proxies:
        self.log.error('No proxies for %s.%s', type(self), attr)
    raise AttributeError(NO_PROXIES_MSG.format(cls=type(self), attr=attr))

def __init_subclass__(cls, **keyword_arguments: Any) -> None:
    """Wrap the subclass's own ``__init__`` so its shared instance is initialized once.

    Args:
        **keyword_arguments: Passed on to ``object.__init_subclass__``.

    """
    super().__init_subclass__(**keyword_arguments)
    own_initializer = cls.__dict__.get('__init__')
    if own_initializer is not None:
        # Through type.__setattr__: the subclass's __init__ is replaced by its wrapper, whose
        # signature a type checker cannot match to the base __init__ it overrides
        type.__setattr__(cls, '__init__', _initialize_once(own_initializer))

    if cls not in ResourceManager.__instances__:

Override the default subclasshook to create an interface.

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it).

@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

def __getattr__(self: Self, attr: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    """Get an attribute from the first proxy that has it.

    This method is called when an attribute is not found.

    Args:
        attr: The attribute to get.

    Returns:
        The attribute.

    Raises:
        AttributeError: If no proxy has the attribute (or there are no proxies yet).

    """
    # The proxies themselves are an instance attribute: before __init__ sets them there are
    # none to try (looking them up here would recurse)
    if attr == 'proxies':
        raise AttributeError(MISSING_ATTRIBUTE_MSG.format(cls=type(self), attr=attr))

    # Try each proxy in turn (BUGS.md #198: the lookup returned or raised on the first)
    for proxy in self.proxies:
        try:
            return getattr(proxy, attr)
        except AttributeError:
            continue

    if self.proxies:
        self.log.error('No proxies for %s.%s', type(self), attr)
    raise AttributeError(NO_PROXIES_MSG.format(cls=type(self), attr=attr))

def __init__(self: Self, game: object = None) -> None:
    """Initialize the font manager.

    Args:
        game (object): The game object.

    """
    super().__init__(game=game)
    self.game: Any = game

    # Register pygame.freetype (imported at module top, so always available)
    pygame.freetype.init()
    log.info('Freetype Font Cache Size: %s', pygame.freetype.get_cache_size())
    log.info(
        'Freetype Font Default Resolution: %s',
        pygame.freetype.get_default_resolution(),
    )

    # Set up the default options.
    FontManager.OPTIONS['font_name'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_name']
    FontManager.OPTIONS['font_size'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_size']
    FontManager.OPTIONS['font_bold'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_bold']
    FontManager.OPTIONS['font_italic'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_italic']
    FontManager.OPTIONS['font_antialias'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_antialias']
    FontManager.OPTIONS['font_dpi'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_dpi']

    # Set font system based on command line argument
    font_system: str = self.game.OPTIONS.get('font_system', 'freetype')
    FontManager.OPTIONS['use_freetype'] = font_system == 'freetype'
    log.info('Font system initialized: %s', font_system)

    pygame.freetype.set_default_resolution(FontManager.OPTIONS['font_dpi'])

    # Ideas:
    #
    # Pre-generate font cache based on settings that are provided.
    # Indexed by the letter they represent.
    # a -> <font name>
    # What about bold, italic, bold + italic, anti-aliased?
    # Maybe we can generate all combinations?
    # Allow caller to pass in a font settings blob and generate.
    # A progress bar class that integrates with tqdm?

    # Ideally, I'd like to support both modes.
    #
    # https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/font.html
    # To use the pygame.freetypeEnhanced pygame module for loading
    # and rendering computer fonts based pygame.ftfont as pygame.fontpygame
    # module for loading and rendering fonts define the environment variable
    # PYGAME_FREETYPE before the first import of pygamethe top level pygame
    # package. Module pygame.ftfont is a pygame.fontpygame module for loading
    # and rendering fonts compatible module that passes all but one of the font
    # module unit tests: it does not have the UCS-2 limitation of the SDL_ttf
    # based font module, so fails to raise an exception for a code point greater
    # than 'uFFFF'. If pygame.freetypeEnhanced pygame module for loading and
    # rendering computer fonts is unavailable then the SDL_ttf font module
    # will be loaded instead.

    # Set up proxies: the font proxy first, then pygame.freetype
    self.proxies: list[Any] = [FontManager.FontProxy(game=game), pygame.freetype]

def __init_subclass__(cls, **keyword_arguments: Any) -> None:
    """Wrap the subclass's own ``__init__`` so its shared instance is initialized once.

    Args:
        **keyword_arguments: Passed on to ``object.__init_subclass__``.

    """
    super().__init_subclass__(**keyword_arguments)
    own_initializer = cls.__dict__.get('__init__')
    if own_initializer is not None:
        # Through type.__setattr__: the subclass's __init__ is replaced by its wrapper, whose
        # signature a type checker cannot match to the base __init__ it overrides
        type.__setattr__(cls, '__init__', _initialize_once(own_initializer))

@classmethod
def args(cls, parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Add font options to the argument parser.

    Args:
        parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The argument parser.

    Returns:
        argparse.ArgumentParser

    """
    group = parser.add_argument_group('Font Options')

    group.add_argument(
        '--font-name',
        default=DEFAULT_FONT_NAME,
        help=(
            f'Font to use (default: the bundled {DEFAULT_FONT_NAME}; the bundled variants are '
            "Vera, VeraBd, VeraIt and VeraBI; any other name is looked up among the system's "
            'fonts)'
        ),
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-size',
        type=int,
        default=14,
        help=(
            'size of the default font, used by text that asks for no font of its own '
            '(default: %(default)s)'
        ),
    )
    # Stored in FontManager.OPTIONS, but no font loader or renderer reads them yet
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-bold',
        action='store_true',
        default=False,
        help='not used yet: stored, but no text is drawn bold because of it',
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-italic',
        action='store_true',
        default=False,
        help='not used yet: stored, but no text is drawn italic because of it',
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-antialias',
        action='store_true',
        default=False,
        help='not used yet: stored, but each text widget chooses its own antialiasing',
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-dpi',
        type=int,
        default=72,
        help=(
            'the resolution, in dots per inch, freetype font sizes are scaled at (sets '
            "pygame.freetype's default resolution); the pygame font system ignores it "
            '(default: %(default)s)'
        ),
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-system',
        choices=['pygame', 'freetype'],
        default='freetype',
        help='Font system to use: freetype (enhanced, default) or pygame (built-in)',
    )

    return parser

@classmethod
def compare_font_systems(
    cls,
    text: str = 'Hello World',
    size: int = 24,
) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Compare both font systems side by side.

    Args:
        text (str): Text to render for comparison.
        size (int): Font size for comparison.

    Returns:
        dict: Information about both font systems.

    """
    config: dict[str, Any] = {'font_size': size}

    # Get pygame.font. Its render takes (text, antialias, color) positionally, not
    # freetype's fgcolor keyword (which raised TypeError on a real pygame.font.Font).
    pygame_font = cast('pygame.font.Font', cls.get_font('pygame', config))
    pygame_surface: pygame.Surface = pygame_font.render(text, True, (255, 255, 255))  # ruff: ignore[boolean-positional-value-in-call]

    # Get pygame.freetype
    freetype_font = cls.get_font('freetype', config)
    freetype_render_result = freetype_font.render(text, fgcolor=(255, 255, 255))
    freetype_surface: pygame.Surface = (
        freetype_render_result[0]
        if isinstance(freetype_render_result, tuple)
        else freetype_render_result
    )

    return {
        'pygame': {
            'font': pygame_font,
            'surface': pygame_surface,
            'size': pygame_surface.get_size(),
            'type': 'pygame.font.Font',
        },
        'freetype': {
            'font': freetype_font,
            'surface': freetype_surface,
            'size': freetype_surface.get_size(),
            'type': 'pygame.freetype.Font',
        },
    }

@classmethod
def font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
    """Return a font object.

    If the font requested can't be found then bitstream_vera will be loaded instead.

    Note that if you are trying to package your game with pyinstaller, you'll need to bundle
    your game's fonts with the pyinstaller invocation.  Make sure you have distribution
    rights to the fonts you're including with your game.

    bitstream_vera is a permissively licensed font that can be used with your game.

    Args:
        font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

    Returns:
        GameFont

    """
    if not font_config:
        font_config = FontManager.OPTIONS

    # Provide default font configuration if not set
    if 'font_name' not in font_config:
        font_config['font_name'] = DEFAULT_FONT_NAME
    if 'font_size' not in font_config:
        font_config['font_size'] = 14

    # Create cache key
    cache_key = f'{font_config["font_name"]}_{font_config["font_size"]}'

    # Check cache first
    if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
        return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

    log.info('Loading Font: %s', font_config['font_name'])
    log.info('Font Size: %s', font_config['font_size'])

    # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
    font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=font_config['font_name'])
    if font_path is not None:
        loaded_font: GameFont = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.freetype.Font(file=font_path, size=font_config['font_size']),
        )
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    try:
        loaded_font = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.freetype.SysFont(
                name=font_config['font_name'],
                size=font_config['font_size'],
            ),
        )
    except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
        # Note: Not sure why but pygame.freetype.SysFont doesn't
        # seem to work with pyinstaller packaged games.
        log.info('Loading Font: Built-In')

        # BUG: pygame's documentation claims that passing None as the font name
        # will load the default font, but this raises TypeError ("not a file object")
        # in PyInstaller-packaged games. Load the bundled Vera.ttf instead.
        # (BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY says where bitmappy.spec bundles it.) The fallback keeps
        # the requested size (it used to load at 12 whatever was asked for).
        loaded_font = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.freetype.Font(
                file=BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY / BUNDLED_FONT_FILE_NAMES['vera'],
                size=font_config['font_size'],
            ),
        )

    # Cache the result
    FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
    return loaded_font

@classmethod
def get_font(
    cls,
    font_system: Literal['pygame', 'freetype'] | None = None,
    font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> GameFont:
    """Get a font object, choosing between pygame.font and pygame.freetype.

    Args:
        font_system: Either "pygame" or "freetype". If None, use the default preference.
        font_config: The font configuration.

    Returns:
        pygame.font.Font | pygame.freetype.Font: The requested font object.

    """
    if font_system is None:
        # Default to freetype
        use_freetype: bool = bool(FontManager.OPTIONS.get('use_freetype', True))
    else:
        use_freetype = font_system == 'freetype'

    # Try freetype first, fall back to pygame if it fails
    if use_freetype:
        try:
            return cls.font(font_config)
        except (TypeError, FileNotFoundError, OSError) as e:
            log.info('Freetype font failed, falling back to pygame: %s', e)
            return cls.pygame_font(font_config)
    else:
        return cls.pygame_font(font_config)

    Returns:
        GameFont: A regular pygame font object.

    """
    if not font_config:
        font_config = FontManager.OPTIONS

    # Provide default font configuration if not set
    if 'font_name' not in font_config:
        font_config['font_name'] = DEFAULT_FONT_NAME
    if 'font_size' not in font_config:
        font_config['font_size'] = 14

    # Create cache key for pygame fonts
    cache_key = f'pygame_{font_config["font_name"]}_{font_config["font_size"]}'

    # Check cache first
    if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
        return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

    # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
    font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=font_config['font_name'])
    if font_path is not None:
        loaded_font: GameFont = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.font.Font(font_path, font_config['font_size']),
        )
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    try:
        # Try to load system font
        loaded_font = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.font.SysFont(font_config['font_name'], font_config['font_size']),
        )
    except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
        # Fall back to default font
        loaded_font = cast('GameFont', pygame.font.Font(None, font_config['font_size']))

    # Cache the result
    FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
    return loaded_font

@classmethod
def release_shared_instances(cls) -> None:
    """Forget every shared instance, so the next construction of each class makes a new one.

    ``GameEngine`` calls it before it makes its event managers: a new engine run builds
    managers of its own (opening devices through its own doors), not the earlier run's.
    """
    ResourceManager.__instances__.clear()

class GameFont(Protocol):
    """Protocol describing the font interface used throughout GlitchyGames.

    Both pygame.font.Font and pygame.freetype.Font satisfy this protocol.
    """

    def render(
        self,
        text: str,
        fgcolor: tuple[int, ...] = ...,
        bgcolor: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> pygame.Surface | tuple[pygame.Surface, pygame.Rect]:
        """Render text to a surface."""
        ...

    def render_to(
        self,
        surf: pygame.Surface,
        dest: tuple[int, int],
        text: str,
        fgcolor: tuple[int, ...] = ...,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> pygame.Rect:
        """Render text directly onto a surface."""
        ...

    def get_rect(self, text: str, **kwargs: Any) -> pygame.Rect:
        """Get the bounding rectangle for rendered text."""
        ...

    def get_linesize(self) -> int:
        """Get the line height for the font."""
        ...

    def size(self, text: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Get the size of rendered text."""
        ...

class FontManager(ResourceManager):
    """A font manager for handling fonts in the game.

    Supports both pygame.font and pygame.freetype font systems:

    Examples:
        # Use default font system (pygame.font)
        font = FontManager.get_font()

        # Force pygame.font
        font = FontManager.get_font(use_freetype=False)

        # Force pygame.freetype
        font = FontManager.get_font(use_freetype=True)

        # Change default system
        FontManager.set_font_system(use_freetype=True)
        font = FontManager.get_font()  # Now uses freetype by default

        # Check current system
        system = FontManager.get_font_system()  # Returns "pygame" or "freetype"

    """

    OPTIONS: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {}
    RENDER_CACHE: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {}
    _font_cache: ClassVar[dict[str, GameFont]] = {}

    class FontProxy(FontEvents, ResourceManager):
        """A font proxy."""

        # A proxy belongs to its manager: each construction is a new one (ResourceManager)
        SHARES_INSTANCE: ClassVar[bool] = False

        def __init__(self: Self, game: object = None) -> None:
            """Initialize the font proxy.

            Args:
                game (object): The game object.

            """
            super().__init__(game=game)
            self.game: Any = game
            self.proxies: list[Any] = [self.game, pygame.freetype]

        @override
        def on_font_changed_event(self: Self, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
            """Handle font changed event.

            Args:
                event (pygame.event.Event): The event to handle.

            """
            self.game.on_font_changed_event(event)

    def __init__(self: Self, game: object = None) -> None:
        """Initialize the font manager.

        Args:
            game (object): The game object.

        """
        super().__init__(game=game)
        self.game: Any = game

        # Register pygame.freetype (imported at module top, so always available)
        pygame.freetype.init()
        log.info('Freetype Font Cache Size: %s', pygame.freetype.get_cache_size())
        log.info(
            'Freetype Font Default Resolution: %s',
            pygame.freetype.get_default_resolution(),
        )

        # Set up the default options.
        FontManager.OPTIONS['font_name'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_name']
        FontManager.OPTIONS['font_size'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_size']
        FontManager.OPTIONS['font_bold'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_bold']
        FontManager.OPTIONS['font_italic'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_italic']
        FontManager.OPTIONS['font_antialias'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_antialias']
        FontManager.OPTIONS['font_dpi'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_dpi']

        # Set font system based on command line argument
        font_system: str = self.game.OPTIONS.get('font_system', 'freetype')
        FontManager.OPTIONS['use_freetype'] = font_system == 'freetype'
        log.info('Font system initialized: %s', font_system)

        pygame.freetype.set_default_resolution(FontManager.OPTIONS['font_dpi'])

        # Ideas:
        #
        # Pre-generate font cache based on settings that are provided.
        # Indexed by the letter they represent.
        # a -> <font name>
        # What about bold, italic, bold + italic, anti-aliased?
        # Maybe we can generate all combinations?
        # Allow caller to pass in a font settings blob and generate.
        # A progress bar class that integrates with tqdm?

        # Ideally, I'd like to support both modes.
        #
        # https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/font.html
        # To use the pygame.freetypeEnhanced pygame module for loading
        # and rendering computer fonts based pygame.ftfont as pygame.fontpygame
        # module for loading and rendering fonts define the environment variable
        # PYGAME_FREETYPE before the first import of pygamethe top level pygame
        # package. Module pygame.ftfont is a pygame.fontpygame module for loading
        # and rendering fonts compatible module that passes all but one of the font
        # module unit tests: it does not have the UCS-2 limitation of the SDL_ttf
        # based font module, so fails to raise an exception for a code point greater
        # than 'uFFFF'. If pygame.freetypeEnhanced pygame module for loading and
        # rendering computer fonts is unavailable then the SDL_ttf font module
        # will be loaded instead.

        # Set up proxies: the font proxy first, then pygame.freetype
        self.proxies: list[Any] = [FontManager.FontProxy(game=game), pygame.freetype]

    @classmethod
    def args(cls, parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
        """Add font options to the argument parser.

        Args:
            parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The argument parser.

        Returns:
            argparse.ArgumentParser

        """
        group = parser.add_argument_group('Font Options')

        group.add_argument(
            '--font-name',
            default=DEFAULT_FONT_NAME,
            help=(
                f'Font to use (default: the bundled {DEFAULT_FONT_NAME}; the bundled variants are '
                "Vera, VeraBd, VeraIt and VeraBI; any other name is looked up among the system's "
                'fonts)'
            ),
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-size',
            type=int,
            default=14,
            help=(
                'size of the default font, used by text that asks for no font of its own '
                '(default: %(default)s)'
            ),
        )
        # Stored in FontManager.OPTIONS, but no font loader or renderer reads them yet
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-bold',
            action='store_true',
            default=False,
            help='not used yet: stored, but no text is drawn bold because of it',
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-italic',
            action='store_true',
            default=False,
            help='not used yet: stored, but no text is drawn italic because of it',
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-antialias',
            action='store_true',
            default=False,
            help='not used yet: stored, but each text widget chooses its own antialiasing',
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-dpi',
            type=int,
            default=72,
            help=(
                'the resolution, in dots per inch, freetype font sizes are scaled at (sets '
                "pygame.freetype's default resolution); the pygame font system ignores it "
                '(default: %(default)s)'
            ),
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-system',
            choices=['pygame', 'freetype'],
            default='freetype',
            help='Font system to use: freetype (enhanced, default) or pygame (built-in)',
        )

        return parser

    # PyInstaller-compiled games fall back to the bundled Vera.ttf font
    # since system font paths are not available in frozen environments.
    @classmethod
    def font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
        """Return a font object.

        If the font requested can't be found then bitstream_vera will be loaded instead.

        Note that if you are trying to package your game with pyinstaller, you'll need to bundle
        your game's fonts with the pyinstaller invocation.  Make sure you have distribution
        rights to the fonts you're including with your game.

        bitstream_vera is a permissively licensed font that can be used with your game.

        Args:
            font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

        Returns:
            GameFont

        """
        if not font_config:
            font_config = FontManager.OPTIONS

        # Provide default font configuration if not set
        if 'font_name' not in font_config:
            font_config['font_name'] = DEFAULT_FONT_NAME
        if 'font_size' not in font_config:
            font_config['font_size'] = 14

        # Create cache key
        cache_key = f'{font_config["font_name"]}_{font_config["font_size"]}'

        # Check cache first
        if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
            return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

        log.info('Loading Font: %s', font_config['font_name'])
        log.info('Font Size: %s', font_config['font_size'])

        # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
        font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=font_config['font_name'])
        if font_path is not None:
            loaded_font: GameFont = cast(
                'GameFont',
                pygame.freetype.Font(file=font_path, size=font_config['font_size']),
            )
            FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
            return loaded_font

        try:
            loaded_font = cast(
                'GameFont',
                pygame.freetype.SysFont(
                    name=font_config['font_name'],
                    size=font_config['font_size'],
                ),
            )
        except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
            # Note: Not sure why but pygame.freetype.SysFont doesn't
            # seem to work with pyinstaller packaged games.
            log.info('Loading Font: Built-In')

            # BUG: pygame's documentation claims that passing None as the font name
            # will load the default font, but this raises TypeError ("not a file object")
            # in PyInstaller-packaged games. Load the bundled Vera.ttf instead.
            # (BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY says where bitmappy.spec bundles it.) The fallback keeps
            # the requested size (it used to load at 12 whatever was asked for).
            loaded_font = cast(
                'GameFont',
                pygame.freetype.Font(
                    file=BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY / BUNDLED_FONT_FILE_NAMES['vera'],
                    size=font_config['font_size'],
                ),
            )

        # Cache the result
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    @classmethod
    def pygame_font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
        """Return a regular pygame font object for compatibility with UI components.

        Args:
            font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

        Returns:
            GameFont: A regular pygame font object.

        """
        if not font_config:
            font_config = FontManager.OPTIONS

        # Provide default font configuration if not set
        if 'font_name' not in font_config:
            font_config['font_name'] = DEFAULT_FONT_NAME
        if 'font_size' not in font_config:
            font_config['font_size'] = 14

        # Create cache key for pygame fonts
        cache_key = f'pygame_{font_config["font_name"]}_{font_config["font_size"]}'

        # Check cache first
        if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
            return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

        # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
        font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=font_config['font_name'])
        if font_path is not None:
            loaded_font: GameFont = cast(
                'GameFont',
                pygame.font.Font(font_path, font_config['font_size']),
            )
            FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
            return loaded_font

        try:
            # Try to load system font
            loaded_font = cast(
                'GameFont',
                pygame.font.SysFont(font_config['font_name'], font_config['font_size']),
            )
        except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
            # Fall back to default font
            loaded_font = cast('GameFont', pygame.font.Font(None, font_config['font_size']))

        # Cache the result
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    @classmethod
    def get_font(
        cls,
        font_system: Literal['pygame', 'freetype'] | None = None,
        font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> GameFont:
        """Get a font object, choosing between pygame.font and pygame.freetype.

        Args:
            font_system: Either "pygame" or "freetype". If None, use the default preference.
            font_config: The font configuration.

        Returns:
            pygame.font.Font | pygame.freetype.Font: The requested font object.

        """
        if font_system is None:
            # Default to freetype
            use_freetype: bool = bool(FontManager.OPTIONS.get('use_freetype', True))
        else:
            use_freetype = font_system == 'freetype'

        # Try freetype first, fall back to pygame if it fails
        if use_freetype:
            try:
                return cls.font(font_config)
            except (TypeError, FileNotFoundError, OSError) as e:
                log.info('Freetype font failed, falling back to pygame: %s', e)
                return cls.pygame_font(font_config)
        else:
            return cls.pygame_font(font_config)

    @classmethod
    def set_font_system(cls, font_system: Literal['pygame', 'freetype']) -> None:
        """Set the default font system preference.

        Args:
            font_system: Either "pygame" or "freetype" to specify the font system.

        """
        FontManager.OPTIONS['use_freetype'] = font_system == 'freetype'
        log.info('Font system set to: %s', font_system)

    @classmethod
    def get_font_system(cls) -> str:
        """Get the current font system preference.

        Returns:
            str: "freetype" or "pygame" indicating the current font system.

        """
        return 'freetype' if FontManager.OPTIONS.get('use_freetype', False) else 'pygame'

    @classmethod
    def compare_font_systems(
        cls,
        text: str = 'Hello World',
        size: int = 24,
    ) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        """Compare both font systems side by side.

        Args:
            text (str): Text to render for comparison.
            size (int): Font size for comparison.

        Returns:
            dict: Information about both font systems.

        """
        config: dict[str, Any] = {'font_size': size}

        # Get pygame.font. Its render takes (text, antialias, color) positionally, not
        # freetype's fgcolor keyword (which raised TypeError on a real pygame.font.Font).
        pygame_font = cast('pygame.font.Font', cls.get_font('pygame', config))
        pygame_surface: pygame.Surface = pygame_font.render(text, True, (255, 255, 255))  # ruff: ignore[boolean-positional-value-in-call]

        # Get pygame.freetype
        freetype_font = cls.get_font('freetype', config)
        freetype_render_result = freetype_font.render(text, fgcolor=(255, 255, 255))
        freetype_surface: pygame.Surface = (
            freetype_render_result[0]
            if isinstance(freetype_render_result, tuple)
            else freetype_render_result
        )

        return {
            'pygame': {
                'font': pygame_font,
                'surface': pygame_surface,
                'size': pygame_surface.get_size(),
                'type': 'pygame.font.Font',
            },
            'freetype': {
                'font': freetype_font,
                'surface': freetype_surface,
                'size': freetype_surface.get_size(),
                'type': 'pygame.freetype.Font',
            },
        }

def __getattr__(self: Self, attr: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    """Get an attribute from the first proxy that has it.

    This method is called when an attribute is not found.

    Args:
        attr: The attribute to get.

    Returns:
        The attribute.

    Raises:
        AttributeError: If no proxy has the attribute (or there are no proxies yet).

    """
    # The proxies themselves are an instance attribute: before __init__ sets them there are
    # none to try (looking them up here would recurse)
    if attr == 'proxies':
        raise AttributeError(MISSING_ATTRIBUTE_MSG.format(cls=type(self), attr=attr))

    # Try each proxy in turn (BUGS.md #198: the lookup returned or raised on the first)
    for proxy in self.proxies:
        try:
            return getattr(proxy, attr)
        except AttributeError:
            continue

    if self.proxies:
        self.log.error('No proxies for %s.%s', type(self), attr)
    raise AttributeError(NO_PROXIES_MSG.format(cls=type(self), attr=attr))

def __init_subclass__(cls, **keyword_arguments: Any) -> None:
    """Wrap the subclass's own ``__init__`` so its shared instance is initialized once.

    Args:
        **keyword_arguments: Passed on to ``object.__init_subclass__``.

    """
    super().__init_subclass__(**keyword_arguments)
    own_initializer = cls.__dict__.get('__init__')
    if own_initializer is not None:
        # Through type.__setattr__: the subclass's __init__ is replaced by its wrapper, whose
        # signature a type checker cannot match to the base __init__ it overrides
        type.__setattr__(cls, '__init__', _initialize_once(own_initializer))

def __new__(cls: type[Self], *_args: Any, **_kwargs: Any) -> Self:
    """Return the class's shared instance, or a new instance for an unshared class.

    Args:
        cls: The class.
        *_args: The positional arguments (``__init__`` takes them).
        **_kwargs: The keyword arguments (``__init__`` takes them).

    Returns:
        The shared instance (made now if there is none yet), or a new instance.

    """
    if not cls.SHARES_INSTANCE:
        return object.__new__(cls)
    if cls not in ResourceManager.__instances__:
        ResourceManager.__instances__[cls] = object.__new__(cls)
        LOG.debug('Created Resource Manager: %s', cls)

    return ResourceManager.__instances__[cls]
__subclasshook__(subclass) classmethod #

Override the default subclasshook to create an interface.

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it).

Returns:
  • bool( bool ) –

    True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

def release_shared_instances(cls) -> None:

def __init__(self: Self, game: object = None) -> None:
    """Initialize the font manager.

    Args:
        game (object): The game object.

    """
    super().__init__(game=game)
    self.game: Any = game

    # Register pygame.freetype (imported at module top, so always available)
    pygame.freetype.init()
    log.info('Freetype Font Cache Size: %s', pygame.freetype.get_cache_size())
    log.info(
        'Freetype Font Default Resolution: %s',
        pygame.freetype.get_default_resolution(),
    )

    # Set up the default options.
    FontManager.OPTIONS['font_name'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_name']
    FontManager.OPTIONS['font_size'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_size']
    FontManager.OPTIONS['font_bold'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_bold']
    FontManager.OPTIONS['font_italic'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_italic']
    FontManager.OPTIONS['font_antialias'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_antialias']
    FontManager.OPTIONS['font_dpi'] = self.game.OPTIONS['font_dpi']

    # Set font system based on command line argument
    font_system: str = self.game.OPTIONS.get('font_system', 'freetype')
    FontManager.OPTIONS['use_freetype'] = font_system == 'freetype'
    log.info('Font system initialized: %s', font_system)

    pygame.freetype.set_default_resolution(FontManager.OPTIONS['font_dpi'])

    # Ideas:
    #
    # Pre-generate font cache based on settings that are provided.
    # Indexed by the letter they represent.
    # a -> <font name>
    # What about bold, italic, bold + italic, anti-aliased?
    # Maybe we can generate all combinations?
    # Allow caller to pass in a font settings blob and generate.
    # A progress bar class that integrates with tqdm?

    # Ideally, I'd like to support both modes.
    #
    # https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/font.html
    # To use the pygame.freetypeEnhanced pygame module for loading
    # and rendering computer fonts based pygame.ftfont as pygame.fontpygame
    # module for loading and rendering fonts define the environment variable
    # PYGAME_FREETYPE before the first import of pygamethe top level pygame
    # package. Module pygame.ftfont is a pygame.fontpygame module for loading
    # and rendering fonts compatible module that passes all but one of the font
    # module unit tests: it does not have the UCS-2 limitation of the SDL_ttf
    # based font module, so fails to raise an exception for a code point greater
    # than 'uFFFF'. If pygame.freetypeEnhanced pygame module for loading and
    # rendering computer fonts is unavailable then the SDL_ttf font module
    # will be loaded instead.

    # Set up proxies: the font proxy first, then pygame.freetype
    self.proxies: list[Any] = [FontManager.FontProxy(game=game), pygame.freetype]

@classmethod
def args(cls, parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Add font options to the argument parser.

    Args:
        parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The argument parser.

    Returns:
        argparse.ArgumentParser

    """
    group = parser.add_argument_group('Font Options')

    group.add_argument(
        '--font-name',
        default=DEFAULT_FONT_NAME,
        help=(
            f'Font to use (default: the bundled {DEFAULT_FONT_NAME}; the bundled variants are '
            "Vera, VeraBd, VeraIt and VeraBI; any other name is looked up among the system's "
            'fonts)'
        ),
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-size',
        type=int,
        default=14,
        help=(
            'size of the default font, used by text that asks for no font of its own '
            '(default: %(default)s)'
        ),
    )
    # Stored in FontManager.OPTIONS, but no font loader or renderer reads them yet
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-bold',
        action='store_true',
        default=False,
        help='not used yet: stored, but no text is drawn bold because of it',
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-italic',
        action='store_true',
        default=False,
        help='not used yet: stored, but no text is drawn italic because of it',
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-antialias',
        action='store_true',
        default=False,
        help='not used yet: stored, but each text widget chooses its own antialiasing',
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-dpi',
        type=int,
        default=72,
        help=(
            'the resolution, in dots per inch, freetype font sizes are scaled at (sets '
            "pygame.freetype's default resolution); the pygame font system ignores it "
            '(default: %(default)s)'
        ),
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-system',
        choices=['pygame', 'freetype'],
        default='freetype',
        help='Font system to use: freetype (enhanced, default) or pygame (built-in)',
    )

    return parser

@classmethod
def compare_font_systems(
    cls,
    text: str = 'Hello World',
    size: int = 24,
) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Compare both font systems side by side.

    Args:
        text (str): Text to render for comparison.
        size (int): Font size for comparison.

    Returns:
        dict: Information about both font systems.

    """
    config: dict[str, Any] = {'font_size': size}

    # Get pygame.font. Its render takes (text, antialias, color) positionally, not
    # freetype's fgcolor keyword (which raised TypeError on a real pygame.font.Font).
    pygame_font = cast('pygame.font.Font', cls.get_font('pygame', config))
    pygame_surface: pygame.Surface = pygame_font.render(text, True, (255, 255, 255))  # ruff: ignore[boolean-positional-value-in-call]

    # Get pygame.freetype
    freetype_font = cls.get_font('freetype', config)
    freetype_render_result = freetype_font.render(text, fgcolor=(255, 255, 255))
    freetype_surface: pygame.Surface = (
        freetype_render_result[0]
        if isinstance(freetype_render_result, tuple)
        else freetype_render_result
    )

    return {
        'pygame': {
            'font': pygame_font,
            'surface': pygame_surface,
            'size': pygame_surface.get_size(),
            'type': 'pygame.font.Font',
        },
        'freetype': {
            'font': freetype_font,
            'surface': freetype_surface,
            'size': freetype_surface.get_size(),
            'type': 'pygame.freetype.Font',
        },
    }

@classmethod
def font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
    """Return a font object.

    If the font requested can't be found then bitstream_vera will be loaded instead.

    Note that if you are trying to package your game with pyinstaller, you'll need to bundle
    your game's fonts with the pyinstaller invocation.  Make sure you have distribution
    rights to the fonts you're including with your game.

    bitstream_vera is a permissively licensed font that can be used with your game.

    Args:
        font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

    Returns:
        GameFont

    """
    if not font_config:
        font_config = FontManager.OPTIONS

    # Provide default font configuration if not set
    if 'font_name' not in font_config:
        font_config['font_name'] = DEFAULT_FONT_NAME
    if 'font_size' not in font_config:
        font_config['font_size'] = 14

    # Create cache key
    cache_key = f'{font_config["font_name"]}_{font_config["font_size"]}'

    # Check cache first
    if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
        return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

    log.info('Loading Font: %s', font_config['font_name'])
    log.info('Font Size: %s', font_config['font_size'])

    # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
    font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=font_config['font_name'])
    if font_path is not None:
        loaded_font: GameFont = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.freetype.Font(file=font_path, size=font_config['font_size']),
        )
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    try:
        loaded_font = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.freetype.SysFont(
                name=font_config['font_name'],
                size=font_config['font_size'],
            ),
        )
    except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
        # Note: Not sure why but pygame.freetype.SysFont doesn't
        # seem to work with pyinstaller packaged games.
        log.info('Loading Font: Built-In')

        # BUG: pygame's documentation claims that passing None as the font name
        # will load the default font, but this raises TypeError ("not a file object")
        # in PyInstaller-packaged games. Load the bundled Vera.ttf instead.
        # (BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY says where bitmappy.spec bundles it.) The fallback keeps
        # the requested size (it used to load at 12 whatever was asked for).
        loaded_font = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.freetype.Font(
                file=BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY / BUNDLED_FONT_FILE_NAMES['vera'],
                size=font_config['font_size'],
            ),
        )

    # Cache the result
    FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
    return loaded_font

@classmethod
def get_font(
    cls,
    font_system: Literal['pygame', 'freetype'] | None = None,
    font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> GameFont:
    """Get a font object, choosing between pygame.font and pygame.freetype.

    Args:
        font_system: Either "pygame" or "freetype". If None, use the default preference.
        font_config: The font configuration.

    Returns:
        pygame.font.Font | pygame.freetype.Font: The requested font object.

    """
    if font_system is None:
        # Default to freetype
        use_freetype: bool = bool(FontManager.OPTIONS.get('use_freetype', True))
    else:
        use_freetype = font_system == 'freetype'

    # Try freetype first, fall back to pygame if it fails
    if use_freetype:
        try:
            return cls.font(font_config)
        except (TypeError, FileNotFoundError, OSError) as e:
            log.info('Freetype font failed, falling back to pygame: %s', e)
            return cls.pygame_font(font_config)
    else:
        return cls.pygame_font(font_config)

@classmethod
def pygame_font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
    """Return a regular pygame font object for compatibility with UI components.

    Args:
        font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

    Returns:
        GameFont: A regular pygame font object.

    """
    if not font_config:
        font_config = FontManager.OPTIONS

    # Provide default font configuration if not set
    if 'font_name' not in font_config:
        font_config['font_name'] = DEFAULT_FONT_NAME
    if 'font_size' not in font_config:
        font_config['font_size'] = 14

    # Create cache key for pygame fonts
    cache_key = f'pygame_{font_config["font_name"]}_{font_config["font_size"]}'

    # Check cache first
    if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
        return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

    # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
    font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=font_config['font_name'])
    if font_path is not None:
        loaded_font: GameFont = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.font.Font(font_path, font_config['font_size']),
        )
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    try:
        # Try to load system font
        loaded_font = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.font.SysFont(font_config['font_name'], font_config['font_size']),
        )
    except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
        # Fall back to default font
        loaded_font = cast('GameFont', pygame.font.Font(None, font_config['font_size']))

    # Cache the result
    FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
    return loaded_font

@classmethod
def release_shared_instances(cls) -> None:
    """Forget every shared instance, so the next construction of each class makes a new one.

    ``GameEngine`` calls it before it makes its event managers: a new engine run builds
    managers of its own (opening devices through its own doors), not the earlier run's.
    """
    ResourceManager.__instances__.clear()

@runtime_checkable
class GameFont(Protocol):
    """Protocol describing the font interface used throughout GlitchyGames.

    Both pygame.font.Font and pygame.freetype.Font satisfy this protocol.
    """

    def render(
        self,
        text: str,
        fgcolor: tuple[int, ...] = ...,
        bgcolor: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> pygame.Surface | tuple[pygame.Surface, pygame.Rect]:
        """Render text to a surface."""
        ...

    def render_to(
        self,
        surf: pygame.Surface,
        dest: tuple[int, int],
        text: str,
        fgcolor: tuple[int, ...] = ...,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> pygame.Rect:
        """Render text directly onto a surface."""
        ...

    def get_rect(self, text: str, **kwargs: Any) -> pygame.Rect:
        """Get the bounding rectangle for rendered text."""
        ...

    def get_linesize(self) -> int:
        """Get the line height for the font."""
        ...

    def size(self, text: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Get the size of rendered text."""
        ...

def bundled_font_path(*, font_name: str) -> Path | None:
    """Return the file of a bundled font, or None when the name is not a bundled font.

    Args:
        font_name: A font name, in any case (e.g. 'Vera', 'VeraBd').

    Returns:
        The bundled font's file, or None for any other name (a system font).

    """
    file_name = BUNDLED_FONT_FILE_NAMES.get(font_name.lower())
    if file_name is None:
        return None
    return BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY / file_name
